criteria.name: Squat depth: hip crease below top of kneecap

sources.says: Depth landmarks are the top of the patella and the hip joint as seen at the apex of the shorts crease; the hip side must drop below parallel with the ground.
Correct means deep, with the hips dropping below level with the top of the patellas; any squat that is not deep is a partial squat.
Thigh undersurface parallel to the floor is often confused with parallel; parallel is defined by the Figure 2-1 landmarks.
Do not accept anything less than full depth.

criteria.name: Bar stays over the middle of the foot

sources.says: The lifter-barbell system is in balance when the bar is directly over the midfoot; at light weights the bar may sit slightly forward and comes over the midfoot as weight increases.
Good technique is the ability to keep the bar vertically aligned with the balance point.
Weight should stay balanced over the middle of the feet; flopping forward lets the bar drop forward of the midfoot.

criteria.name: Bar path is a vertical line

sources.says: Gravity acts straight down, so a straight vertical line is the most efficient bar path.
Horizontal bar movement is not work against gravity.

criteria.name: Back angle about 45 degrees at the bottom

sources.says: At the bottom the back is inclined at about 45 degrees, not at all vertical, which places the bar over the midfoot.
Balance problems usually indicate a back angle that is too vertical; sit back and lean forward enough.

sources.ref: Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong: Back angle
sources.says: The back is usually too vertical (wrong mental picture or bar too high) or too horizontal (chest not kept up).

criteria.name: Hip drive: hips go up, not forward; chest does not lead

sources.says: Come up by driving your butt straight up in the air - up, not forward - keeping weight over the whole foot.
The back angle during the drive up is critical; flopping forward allows the bar to drop forward of the midfoot.

sources.ref: Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong: Hip drive
sources.says: Lifting the chest instead of driving the hips up makes the back angle too vertical and kills power out of the bottom.

criteria.name: Knees just a little in front of the toes at the bottom

sources.says: At the bottom the knees are just a little in front of the toes, feet flat, hips back.
Partial squats push the knees far forward of the midfoot; the low-bar squat keeps the knees back.
Your feet are flat on the floor.
Assume the bottom position with knees out, toes out and heels down.
Don't stop at the bottom - go down and immediately come back up.
Tight posterior muscles at the bottom give a slight rebound (stretch reflex).
Looking up interferes with the bottom position, hip drive and chest position, and overextends the neck.
Fix the eyes on the floor 4-5 feet in front of you.

sources.ref: Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong: Eye gaze
sources.says: Failing to look down kills hip drive.

criteria.name: Bar low on the back (just below the spine of the scapula)

sources.says: The bar should sit in the lowest secure position, just below the spine of the scapula.
Most people starting out place the bar too high, just above the scapular spine instead of just below it.

sources.ref: Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong: Bar placement
sources.says: Placing the bar too high affects back angle and hip drive.

not_assessable.why: Needs a front or overhead view.
Foot rotation is not visible from the side.

not_assessable.topic: Knees shoved out, thighs parallel to the feet
not_assessable.why: Sideways knee travel is perpendicular to the camera.

not_assessable.topic: Back flat, held in lumbar and thoracic extension
not_assessable.why: Spine curvature is not captured by joint keypoints.

not_assessable.topic: Grip width, thumbs on top, straight wrists
not_assessable.why: Hands are small and usually occluded by the plates.

not_assessable.topic: Elbows up, chest up to trap the bar
not_assessable.why: Not reliably visible from the side.

not_assessable.topic: Unracking with both feet under the bar; one step back
Big breath held during the rep
Sets of five, empty-bar warm-up, weight increments

findings.criterion: Squat depth: hip crease below top of kneecap

sources.says: Depth landmarks are the top of the patella and the hip joint as seen at the apex of the shorts crease; the hip side must drop below parallel with the ground.
Correct means deep, with the hips dropping below level with the top of the patellas; any squat that is not deep is a partial squat.
Thigh undersurface parallel to the floor is often confused with parallel; parallel is defined by the Figure 2-1 landmarks.
Do not accept anything less than full depth.

values.unit: thigh lengths (positive = hip keypoint below knee keypoint)
values.band: meets if >= 0.02; fails if < -0.1; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document rule is 'hip crease below top of patella' (no tolerance needed in principle). The band from -0.10 to +0.02 thigh lengths is our allowance for the gap between keypoint centres and the document's surface landmarks.

findings.template_feedback: This rep stopped above parallel. Go all the way down until the crease of your hips is below the top of your kneecaps. The document's usual causes: not looking down, not shoving the knees out, stance too narrow or too wide, or not committing to depth (ref p35).
findings.why_partial: The document defines depth with the hip crease (apex of the shorts crease) and the TOP of the patella. A pose model gives hip-joint and knee-joint centres instead, so we measure a proxy and leave a borderline band where the proxy cannot decide.

findings.criterion: Bar stays over the middle of the foot

sources.says: The lifter-barbell system is in balance when the bar is directly over the midfoot; at light weights the bar may sit slightly forward and comes over the midfoot as weight increases.
Good technique is the ability to keep the bar vertically aligned with the balance point.
Weight should stay balanced over the middle of the feet; flopping forward lets the bar drop forward of the midfoot.

values.unit: foot lengths (largest horizontal distance bar->midfoot during the rep)
values.band: meets if <= 0.2; fails if > 0.35; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document says 'directly over'; it allows some forward offset at light weights but gives no number. 0.20 / 0.35 foot lengths are our bands.

findings.reason: The camera is not square to the side of the lifter, so this measurement would be distorted.
findings.template_feedback: Mark the end of the bar (plate centre) and your heel and toe before analysis so we can check bar balance.
findings.why_partial: Requires the user to mark the plate centre and the heel/toe. Perspective (plate nearer the camera than the foot) adds small error.

findings.criterion: Bar path is a vertical line

sources.says: Gravity acts straight down, so a straight vertical line is the most efficient bar path.
Horizontal bar movement is not work against gravity.

values.unit: foot lengths (max minus min horizontal bar position in the rep)
values.band: meets if <= 0.2; fails if > 0.35; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document says 'straight vertical line'; the allowed drift is our assumption.

findings.reason: The camera is not square to the side of the lifter, so this measurement would be distorted.
findings.template_feedback: Mark the plate centre before analysis to measure the bar path.
findings.why_partial: Requires the bar marker; tracker accuracy is a few pixels.

findings.criterion: Back angle about 45 degrees at the bottom

sources.says: At the bottom the back is inclined at about 45 degrees, not at all vertical, which places the bar over the midfoot.
Balance problems usually indicate a back angle that is too vertical; sit back and lean forward enough.

sources.ref: Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong: Back angle
sources.says: The back is usually too vertical (wrong mental picture or bar too high) or too horizontal (chest not kept up).

values.unit: degrees above horizontal
values.band: meets if 35 to 55; fails if < 28 or > 62; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: The document says 'about 45 degrees' (document number). The +/-10 degree band and the 28/62 failure limits are our assumption.

findings.reason: The camera is not square to the side of the lifter, so this measurement would be distorted.
findings.template_feedback: Shoulder or hip was not visible clearly enough at the bottom to measure your back angle.
findings.why_partial: Uses the shoulder->hip line as a proxy for the plane of the torso.

findings.criterion: Hip drive: hips go up, not forward; chest does not lead

sources.says: Come up by driving your butt straight up in the air - up, not forward - keeping weight over the whole foot.
The back angle during the drive up is critical; flopping forward allows the bar to drop forward of the midfoot.

sources.ref: Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong: Hip drive
sources.says: Lifting the chest instead of driving the hips up makes the back angle too vertical and kills power out of the bottom.

values.unit: degrees (positive = torso became more upright, i.e. chest led)
values.band: meets if -10 to 10; fails if < -15 or > 15; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document: back angle held during the drive. 'Held' within 10 degrees, failure beyond 15, are our assumptions. Early ascent = first 30% of hip rise.

values.unit: thigh lengths the hip moved toward the toes during early ascent
values.band: meets if <= 0.1; fails if > 0.2; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document: 'up, not forward'. The allowed forward hip travel is our assumption.

findings.reason: The camera is not square to the side of the lifter, so this measurement would be distorted.
findings.template_feedback: We could not follow the shoulder and hip clearly out of the bottom of this rep.
findings.why_partial: Inferred from how the back angle and hip position change in the first part of the ascent; muscle recruitment itself cannot be seen.

findings.criterion: Knees just a little in front of the toes at the bottom

sources.says: At the bottom the knees are just a little in front of the toes, feet flat, hips back.
Partial squats push the knees far forward of the midfoot; the low-bar squat keeps the knees back.

values.unit: foot lengths (knee joint centre ahead of the toe tip; negative = behind)
values.band: meets if -0.4 to 0.2; fails if > 0.5; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document: 'just a little in front of your toes'. Because the knee keypoint is ~0.3 foot lengths behind the front of the kneecap, the band is wide and only an extreme forward knee fails.

findings.reason: The camera is not square to the side of the lifter, so this measurement would be distorted.
findings.template_feedback: Mark your toe before analysis, and make sure the knee is visible at the bottom.
findings.why_partial: Needs the toe marker; the knee keypoint is the joint centre, not the front of the knee, so only clear cases get a verdict. 'Knees out' (sideways) cannot be seen from the side.

findings.criterion: Feet stay flat (heels down)

sources.says: Your feet are flat on the floor.
Assume the bottom position with knees out, toes out and heels down.

values.unit: shin lengths the ankle rose above its standing height
values.band: meets if <= 0.03; fails if > 0.08; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document: feet flat. Keypoint jitter allowance (0.03) and failure level (0.08) are our assumptions.

findings.template_feedback: Your feet appeared to stay flat through the rep.
findings.why_partial: The pose model has no heel point; we use rise of the ankle keypoint as a proxy for the heel lifting.

findings.criterion: No stop at the bottom

sources.says: Don't stop at the bottom - go down and immediately come back up.
Tight posterior muscles at the bottom give a slight rebound (stretch reflex).

values.unit: seconds the hip stayed within 3% of a thigh length of its lowest point
values.band: meets if <= 0.5; fails if > 1.0; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document: 'immediately'. 0.5 s / 1.0 s are our assumptions.

findings.reason: Borderline: the measurement is inside the uncertainty band, so the app will not call it either way.
findings.template_feedback: The hip was not tracked well enough at the bottom to time the turnaround.

findings.criterion: Eyes down, chin down

sources.says: Looking up interferes with the bottom position, hip drive and chest position, and overextends the neck.
Fix the eyes on the floor 4-5 feet in front of you.

sources.ref: Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong: Eye gaze
sources.says: Failing to look down kills hip drive.

values.unit: degrees the ear->nose line points below horizontal (negative = looking up)
values.band: meets if >= 10; fails if < -10; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document gives a target (floor 4-5 ft ahead), not a head angle. The head-pitch bands are our assumption and only catch clear looking-up.

findings.reason: The camera is not square to the side of the lifter, so this measurement would be distorted.
findings.template_feedback: The face was not visible clearly enough to estimate head position.
findings.why_partial: Eye direction is not measurable; we use head pitch (ear->nose line) and only call clear cases.

findings.criterion: Bar low on the back (just below the spine of the scapula)

sources.says: The bar should sit in the lowest secure position, just below the spine of the scapula.
Most people starting out place the bar too high, just above the scapular spine instead of just below it.

sources.ref: Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong: Bar placement
sources.says: Placing the bar too high affects back angle and hip drive.

values.unit: torso lengths the bar centre sits above the shoulder keypoint, along the torso
values.band: never awarded 'meets' (not verifiable on video); fails if > 0.15; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Never 'meets' by design (anatomy not visible). Fails only if the bar is clearly high on the traps.

findings.reason: The camera is not square to the side of the lifter, so this measurement would be distorted.
findings.template_feedback: Bar placement on the shoulder blade cannot be confirmed from video; check it by feel - the bar should sit just below the bony ridge (spine of the scapula).
findings.why_partial: The scapular spine is not visible on video. We can only flag a bar that sits clearly above the shoulder joint (high-bar); we never award a pass.

findings.template_feedback: Mark your toe before analysis, and make sure the knee is visible at the bottom.
findings.why_partial: Needs the toe marker; the knee keypoint is the joint centre, not the front of the knee, so only clear cases get a verdict. 'Knees out' (sideways) cannot be seen from the side.

findings.criterion: Feet stay flat (heels down)

sources.says: Your feet are flat on the floor.
Assume the bottom position with knees out, toes out and heels down.

values.unit: shin lengths the ankle rose above its standing height
values.band: meets if <= 0.03; fails if > 0.08; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document: feet flat. Keypoint jitter allowance (0.03) and failure level (0.08) are our assumptions.

findings.reason: Borderline: the measurement is inside the uncertainty band, so the app will not call it either way.
findings.template_feedback: The ankle was not tracked reliably enough to judge whether your heels stayed down.
findings.why_partial: The pose model has no heel point; we use rise of the ankle keypoint as a proxy for the heel lifting.

findings.criterion: No stop at the bottom

sources.says: Don't stop at the bottom - go down and immediately come back up.
Tight posterior muscles at the bottom give a slight rebound (stretch reflex).

values.unit: seconds the hip stayed within 3% of a thigh length of its lowest point
values.band: meets if <= 0.5; fails if > 1.0; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document: 'immediately'. 0.5 s / 1.0 s are our assumptions.

findings.template_feedback: You turned around at the bottom without stopping, using the stretch reflex.

findings.criterion: Eyes down, chin down

sources.says: Looking up interferes with the bottom position, hip drive and chest position, and overextends the neck.
Fix the eyes on the floor 4-5 feet in front of you.

sources.ref: Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong: Eye gaze
sources.says: Failing to look down kills hip drive.

values.unit: degrees the ear->nose line points below horizontal (negative = looking up)
values.band: meets if >= 10; fails if < -10; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Document gives a target (floor 4-5 ft ahead), not a head angle. The head-pitch bands are our assumption and only catch clear looking-up.

findings.reason: The camera is not square to the side of the lifter, so this measurement would be distorted.
findings.template_feedback: The face was not visible clearly enough to estimate head position.
findings.why_partial: Eye direction is not measurable; we use head pitch (ear->nose line) and only call clear cases.

findings.criterion: Bar low on the back (just below the spine of the scapula)

sources.says: The bar should sit in the lowest secure position, just below the spine of the scapula.
Most people starting out place the bar too high, just above the scapular spine instead of just below it.

sources.ref: Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong: Bar placement
sources.says: Placing the bar too high affects back angle and hip drive.

values.unit: torso lengths the bar centre sits above the shoulder keypoint, along the torso
values.band: never awarded 'meets' (not verifiable on video); fails if > 0.15; otherwise borderline
values.tolerance_note: Never 'meets' by design (anatomy not visible). Fails only if the bar is clearly high on the traps.

findings.reason: The camera is not square to the side of the lifter, so this measurement would be distorted.
findings.template_feedback: Bar placement on the shoulder blade cannot be confirmed from video; check it by feel - the bar should sit just below the bony ridge (spine of the scapula).
findings.why_partial: The scapular spine is not visible on video. We can only flag a bar that sits clearly above the shoulder joint (high-bar); we never award a pass.

coaching.headline: 3 reps analysed. Main fix: squat depth.
coaching.summary: Across all reps, 3 checks met the standard, 3 did not, and 24 could not be assessed. Start with: Squat depth: hip crease below top of kneecap.

findings.feedback: This rep stopped above parallel. Go all the way down until the crease of your hips is below the top of your kneecaps. The document's usual causes: not looking down, not shoving the knees out, stance too narrow or too wide, or not committing to depth (ref p35).
findings.uncertainty: The pass/fail band is the app's assumption; the document gives the direction, not a number. The document defines depth with the hip crease (apex of the shorts crease) and the TOP of the patella. A pose model gives hip-joint and knee-joint centres instead, so we measure a proxy and leave a borderline band where the proxy cannot decide.
